answer: Deterministic Falcon Handshake: each agent identity is bound to a fresh random challenge drawn after registration from a public beacon whose pulse is unpredictable in advance. The agent must return a valid Falcon signature over that nonce within a short window; identities that fail are suspended. Because the challenge is post-commitment, cloning cannot precompute answers, so each clone needs its own live signing run. A pigment of the seed rotates the challenge per epoch, forcing per-identity recomputation. Attacker cost: one expensive signing operation plus latency per clone, per epoch.
